one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, paired-comparison study asking what fraction of a procedural-memory bank's accuracy gain over a hand-written instruction survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is trained on the exact same episodes, reporting a single substitution ratio S via a superiority-plus-TOST-equivalence conjunction, with a compiled-bank arm, a whole-bank-dump arm, a co-adaptation arm, and a deliberately non-compilable positive control to certify the instrument can detect non-substitutable value.
closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202), which the proposal itself surfaces and partially concedes to: it already runs Memento, ReasoningBank and GEPA on a shared 528/267 train/test split and reports that no automatic method wins in every cell. That paper establishes the exact three-way template (memory vs. optimizer vs. vanilla on matched trajectories) this proposal is built on, so it substantially narrows the novelty claim. What remains genuinely new is what EvoAgentBench structurally cannot compute — it has no combined optimizer+memory cell, so it cannot answer 'does the memory-vs-none gap shrink once the optimizer has seen the same data,' which is this proposal's actual object. That is a real, if incremental, advance layered on top of an already-published comparison.
strongest_objection: The track explicitly restricts scope to 'small open-weight models (7B-32B class)... the interesting result must not depend on frontier-scale models' and caps resources at 'open-weight models up to ~32B.' The proposal's primary, load-bearing agent A1 is gpt-oss-120b — roughly 4x over that ceiling — chosen specifically because it is where a prior study found a non-null memory effect. The one agent that is actually in scope, Qwen3.5-27B (A2), is pre-registered from the outset as the 'degenerate regime' where the bank has no effect at the hand-written instruction and S is explicitly undefined ('the question is moot'). So the only cells that can answer the paper's central hypothesis (H1∧H2 on A1) run on an out-of-scope model, while the track-compliant model is defined in advance to produce no answer at all. A strict area chair could reject on scope grounds alone, and there is no fallback in the design that tests the substitution claim on any 7B-32B agent where memory actually helps.
what_would_fix_it: Identify or construct at least one 7B-32B-class agent/environment pairing where the ExpeL bank shows a genuine, non-degenerate effect (via the same G1/G6-style precheck already used to screen A1 and A2), and run the primary substitution test there, so the headline claim does not depend on stepping outside the track's stated model-size ceiling. Separately, build the memory artifact in the actual ReasoningBank format (self-judged success/failure distillation), not only ExpeL-style INSIGHT/PROCEDURE/OUTCOME items, since ReasoningBank is repeatedly named as a target system and is what the closest comparator (EvoAgentBench) actually evaluated — without it the reported numbers can't be cross-checked against that benchmark. Given the design already spans 14+ cells x 2 agents x 2 environments plus moderator, iso-cost, and generality analyses, also commit explicitly to the minimal subset that must ship even under the stated contingency cuts, so a reader can see the guaranteed core result independent of the extensions.
missing_baseline: A ReasoningBank-style bank (self-judged success/failure distillation over trajectories), as opposed to the ExpeL-style INSIGHT/PROCEDURE/OUTCOME bank actually built. ReasoningBank is named throughout as one of the 'target' systems and is central to the closest prior work (EvoAgentBench's own ReasoningBank cells), but the experiments never construct one, so the substitution ratio reported here cannot be directly compared to the closest published table's numbers — a reviewer would ask whether the substitution result is specific to ExpeL-style distillation or generalizes to the memory format the field actually benchmarks most.
preprint_collision: The check is procedurally more rigorous than most: it states a dated scan, multiple verification channels (HF Papers queries, by-ID abstract checks, web search), and — unusually — documents a self-correction, reinstating five citations (including TERMS-Bench and MemAPO) that an earlier version of this proposal had wrongly retracted as unverifiable. It also directly names and engages the paper that most threatens novelty (EvoAgentBench, arXiv 2607.05202), withdrawing an explicit prior claim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other.' That is exactly the behavior this instruction is meant to reward. That said, the check cannot be taken at face value: it cites roughly twenty very recent (2026 Q1-Q3) arXiv IDs with unusually precise statistics attached (e.g., '65.7% attributable to procedural anchoring,' 'retrieval precision collapsing from 29.6% to 3.3%'), none of which I can verify, and the process's own admission that a prior scan produced false retractions shows the method is not yet reliable. Net: the collision check is a real, substantive part of the submission rather than a pro forma gesture, but its central defense — that EvoAgentBench lacks the combined cells needed for a substitution test — is the load-bearing claim for this proposal's novelty and rests entirely on preprints I have no way to independently confirm.
